text:
mike: Quick heads-up — I prototyped a header-first routing flow that uses a signed header to assert tenant+route. Calling it `X-Route-Signature`. Idea is: verify signature in edge, route directly to dedicated pools. Avoids brittle UA heuristics. Thoughts? :thinking:

ashley: I'm intrigued. How do you sign it? HMAC? worried about replay and clock skew. Also how does this interact with Authorization header?

mike: HMAC-SHA256 with short TTL, include tenant_id||route_hint||ts. Example: `sig = HMAC(key, tenant|route|ts)` then header: `X-Route-Signature: sig|ts`. Edge verifies via KMS-managed shared key per-customer. Replay mitigated by ts window and seen-nonce cache.

kelly: That would be way cleaner than our current UA-grok rules. But security team will push back on trusting any client-supplied header — how do we prevent spoofing if someone steals a key? :shield:

li: Two notes: (1) we must support fallback to existing routing (UA + X-Customer-Routing) for older clients, (2) telemetry needs to mark which signal matched so we don't lose attribution for billing/quotas.

samir: Agree with li. Also implement precedence rules: X-Route-Signature (verified) > Authorization (when token maps to tenant) > X-Customer-Routing (unsigned hint) > UA-heuristic. That avoids weird edgecases where an old header accidentally overrides a verified identity.

mike: Proposed config fragment for router (pseudo-yaml):

```
route_policy:
  - match: header X-Route-Signature
    verify: true
    verify_via: kms/tenant-keys
    on_verify: route_to: tenant_pool
    fallback: ua_heuristic
  - match: Authorization (token->tenant)
    route_to: tenant_pool
  - match: header X-Customer-Routing
    route_hint: soft
  - match: User-Agent
    heuristic: legacy-routing
```

ashley: From an implementation POV, verifying per-request HMAC at the edge adds CPU. We should batch-accept signed headers only on a subset of edges during canary, or pre-warm a verification cache. Also need metrics: verify_success, verify_fail, fallback_used.

kelly: UX request for the Console: when a request is sampled show a small "routing_reason" column (signed_header | token | hint | ua) and if signed_header, show `tenant_id` + `sig_ts`. It'll make debugging rollouts much easier.

devops-bot: deploy-notice: new router feature flag `signed-header-routing` created by mike. Canaries enabled on 10% of ingress edges.

samir: Quotas/usage impact: if we accept signed routing for tenant pools we must ensure the tenant id in the signature is used for metering (not the client IP or UA). Also consider malicious tenants trying to route into dedicated pools — require tenant config opt-in for dedicated routing.

li: Agree on opt-in. Add server-side enforcement: tenant metadata has `signed_routing: enabled/disabled` and key rotation window. If disabled but header present -> reject or ignore? I'd prefer ignore + metric increment.

mike: Plan: I'll open a design PR with three parts — (1) header verification implementation & caching, (2) routing precedence & config flags, (3) telemetry + console column. Can we decide on fallback semantics now? I lean `ignore if disabled` so old clients don't get unexpected rejections.

ashley: `ignore + metric` seems safest for rollout. After 2 weeks of telemetry we can flip to `reject` for tenants that requested enforcement.

kelly: Also add a debug endpoint for support to validate an `X-Route-Signature` sample (internal RFC-style). Saves a ton of Slack threads.

mike: Sweet. I'll file tasks: design PR, console mock, and support endpoint. Canaries on 10% edges per devops-bot.

li: Assign to mike for PR, samir for quota rules, kelly for console mocks, ashley for perf review.

samir: I'll add a short eval to Ensure billing attribution is consistent in our billing-pipeline when header_source = signed_header.

mike: Thanks all. I'll post the PR link once ready. :thumbsup:
